why: Second round of the L11 flaky-test fix (0036), in next/. The template copy alone ran the law in 52,091 ms on CI (run 44284881776), still near the 60 s bound, so the lead asked for a split that keeps every cut. The storage law is now 16 tests, one per flow, under one @effect/vitest layer that builds the template and the inventory once. Every part runs the same fc.assert (seed 119120, 100 walks, the same picks and the same list of operations still to cut), so every part chooses the old law's cuts in the old order and runs only those in its own flow. Parked until CI runs the split.
note: A throwaway node script copied the law's arbitraries, seed and choice rule and ran no product code. At the measured 901-operation inventory the old law cuts 1,369 times, and the 16 parts' cuts, sorted by walk and step, equal those 1,369 cuts one for one; each part reaches all of its flow's operations. The largest parts are recovery (238 cuts), exit (209), migration (198) and fresh (174). The template copy's inventory, drift and plants were measured by the lead's cloud box at f01509788, before the split: cold and template inventories equal statement by statement in all 16 flows, drift 0, the reply plant 59 leaks and the span plant 172 in each walk, equal line for line, each run twice. Lint and typecheck green; the law file is host-only (0178), so it did not run here.
